subject: Acceptance proving plan and exit simulation checklist
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Beth Connors <beth.connons@healthsync.com>, Procurement <procurement@healthsync.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acceptance proving plan and exit simulation checklist

Hi Beth / HealthSync team,

Thanks for a productive demo last week — excited about the fit. Per our conversation, attached is a concise "Acceptance proving" plan we propose to validate the POC and unblock commercial close. High level: we split the evaluation into three parallel tracks so stakeholders can sign off independently:

1) Functional correctness (Quality)
   - Acceptance test: 1,000 representative queries across 6 scenarios (clinical summary, triage routing, billing code extraction, patient matching, note generation, privacy redaction). Pass gate: >=95% concordance with your labeled set (sampling-based).

2) Performance & reliability (SLO verification)
   - Smoke probes and ramp test: sustained 500 QPS synthetic replay for 1 hour during peak scenario; p99 generation latency <250ms for single-shot inference; end-to-end 95th latency (api->app) <400ms.

3) Security & observability (Compliance evidence)
   - Exit gate: Secure key rotation proof, audit-log export for 7 days, and proof of data partitioning for HealthSync tenant.

We propose a single "exit simulation" day on Dec 17 where we run the scripts in the attached exit-sim-checklist.xlsx and live smoke-probes.md. Suggested owners: Grace -> test harness + evidence collection; Marcus -> SLA sampling + latency dashboard; Lauren -> stakeholder sign-off facilitation and rollback runbook.

Concrete asks for you before Dec 15:
- Confirm the 6 representative scenarios (I attached a suggested CSV).
- Share any restricted PII test fixtures or masking rules we should apply in the run.
- Procurement: note we expect to finalize PO terms in parallel; if there are timing constraints for signing by Dec 24, flag them now.

If that plan looks good I will lock the runbook and circulate a calendar invite for the simulation window (9:00–12:00 PT, Dec 17 and 14:00–17:00 PT as contingency).

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Lead, HealthCare Accounts
Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0127

Attachments: exit-sim-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 sheets), smoke-probes.md (markdown, 12 tests)

From: Beth Connors <beth.connons@healthsync.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@healthsync.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acceptance proving plan and exit simulation checklist

Rishi — thanks for the clear breakdown. A few quick notes from our side: 

- Scenarios: the ones you listed look right but swap out 'note generation' for 'structured medication extraction' (we have a smaller labeled set for that).
- Fixtures: we'll provide a de-identified batch and a policy doc describing what fields must be redacted before the run.
- Timing: Dec 17 is OK for the simulation window. Procurement asked if the PO can be ready to sign by Dec 22; they can't commit before the simulation evidence is collected.

Also: on the latency target — our product team would like a secondary check that p50 stays under 120ms during the smoke (they use p50 in internal dashboards). Not a blocker but helpful.

I'll confirm the labeled sets by EOD Dec 13 and share the redaction policy.

Thanks,
Beth
VP, Product
HealthSync

Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 10:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acceptance proving plan and exit simulation checklist — updated runbook & owners

Beth — appreciate the quick turnaround. Updated plan below (and I uploaded a small revisions sheet to the Drive link). Changes incorporated: medication extraction replaces note generation; added p50 check.

Updated owners & playbook highlights:
- Grace O'Connor (Redwood): instrument test harness, capture per-request telemetry, export raw logs to the shared Drive folder. Responsible for producing the evidence bundle.
- Marcus Lin (Redwood): run SLA sampling analysis post-run (p50/p90/p99), verify p99 <250ms and p50 <120ms for core scenarios.
- Lauren Bishop (Redwood): run stakeholder checklist, trigger rollback if any critical gate fails, and coordinate procurement milestone.

Run windows (two attempts):
- Attempt 1: Dec 17, 09:00–11:30 PT (primary)
- Attempt 2 (fallback): Dec 18, 14:00–16:30 PT

Exit gate decisions (binary pass/fail):
- Quality: sample concordance >=95% across labeled set OR documented, reproducible failure modes with remediation plan.
- Latency: p99 <250ms AND p50 <120ms for at least 5 of the 6 scenarios during primary window.
- Security: audit logs validated and key rotation proof captured.

If any gate fails we follow the rollback matrix in sheet 2 of exit-sim-checklist.xlsx (quick rollback = 1 hour to previous pinned model; full escalation to engineering within 8 hours).

Next steps from the Redwood side by Dec 15: load test harness into your staging environment, schedule a 30-minute dry run with your engineers (recommended Dec 16), and circulate a final sign-off matrix. I'll also drop a DocuSign envelope for the PO pathway so procurement can pre-review terms.

Grace / Marcus / Lauren — flagged you all to confirm you're good with the owners and timing.

Thanks — Rishi

Subject: Re: Acceptance proving plan and exit simulation checklist — simulation complete

Rishi / team — quick note to close the loop. We ran the primary simulation on Dec 17 (Grace's team ran the harness; Marcus handed over the latency report). Highlights:

- Quality: concordance 96.3% across sampled medication extraction and clinical routing scenarios — PASS.
- Latency: p50 = 98ms, p99 = 238ms across the 6 scenario baseline — PASS (met both p50 and p99 gates).
- Security: audit logs exported and rotation proof submitted — PASS.

Procurement: given the pass, we are moving to finalize the PO. Expect routing to legal today and signature next week.

Thanks to the Redwood team for the clear runbook and for being responsive during the window. Beth

--
